html:
A machine on a real plant has a screen beside it. The operator reads it at a glance, sets a temperature, starts and stops, and sees what went wrong last night. In Logix Connect that screen is the Process HMI: an operator terminal you place anywhere on the floor and point at a machine. It shows a live faceplate of a tank, the mix kitchen, a case packer, a camera, an infeed or a whole line; it is a touch screen (a mouse click is a touch) and it works in the top view and in 3D. The Operator View is the same screen as a document tab of its own, full size, with a panel of real-looking buttons beside it.

Placing an HMI and connecting it

  1. In Program mode, Operator → Process HMI in the palette; click the floor to place it.
  2. In its properties, Shows: pick the machine. Left blank, it shows the nearest vessel.
  3. Heater setpoint tag: the controller tag the TEMP page writes, normally a REAL.
  4. START button tag, STOP button tag and Running indicator tag: optional; with them set, START and STOP appear on the MAIN page.
  5. Function keys: up to five more machines, by name. The keys under the screen then switch the terminal between them, so one terminal can run the whole line.
  6. Screen size and Mounting (pedestal or wall bracket) are for the 3D view.

The HMI has no I/O points of its own: it reads the machine directly and writes only the tags you give it. Its properties end in a Connections section that says what it shows and which tags it writes; on a tank, the same section lists every HMI showing it and every pipe in and out.

Touching the screen

The screen answers in Run mode; in Program mode a click selects the part instead, so you can move it. Across the top are the page tabs: MAIN, TEMP (on a vessel with a temperature), RECIPE (on a mix tank) and ALARMS, with a red dot on ALARMS while an alarm is active. The faceplates are drawn the way plant HMIs are (ISA-101 style): a grey screen and dark text, with colour kept for what is running and what is wrong, so a lit heater or a red alarm line stands out because nothing else is bright. Theme → HMI style: classic colour switches to the older, colourful look.

MAIN is the overview: the vessel with its liquid, the HI and LO marks, the state (FILLING, HEAT+MIX, MIXING, DRAINING, HOLDING, EMPTY, PURGING), the temperature, the trend, the share of each ingredient in the batch, what each flowmeter reads and each pump, the heater and the mixer, grey stopped and green running. TEMP has two cards: HEATER SETPOINT, which writes the setpoint tag (what the heater does with it is up to your program), and HIGH LIMIT · THERMOSTAT, the tank’s own thermostat, which is the hardware safety and not the control. Touch a value for the keypad: digits, ., ⌫, CLR, then ENT to write or ESC to leave it. ALARMS lists every Simulator Log line that names this machine, newest first, with anything abnormal in red.

Watch for

If the program writes the same tag on every scan, the operator’s value lasts one scan, and the message line says so in red: the tag has two writers and the program always writes last. Give the operator a tag of their own, and let the program read it.

START and STOP on the screen

Give the HMI a START and a STOP tag (BOOLs) and its MAIN page shows two pushbuttons. A touch pulses the tag: on for a quarter of a second of machine time, then off, so the program sees it for several scans, exactly like a momentary button wired to an input. Give it a Running tag too and START lights green and reads RUNNING while that tag is on. The program has to listen for them, and the plant way is in parallel with the hardwired buttons, never instead of them: the HMI tags are ordinary BOOLs (not aliases of inputs, since a real HMI cannot write an input), and the run rung takes either START and either STOP. Level 7 is set up like that.

[XIC(Start_PB),XIC(HMI_Start),XIC(Run)]XIO(Stop_PB)XIO(HMI_Stop)XIC(E_Stop)OTE(Run);
Try it: three ways to start

On Level 7 with its reference program, start the batch from the console’s Start button, stop it with STOP on Tank_HMI, start it again from the Operator View, and stop it from the console. One seal-in rung, three operator stations. Now delete the HMI_Start branch and press START on the Operator View: the press is logged and the tag pulses (watch it in Quick Watch), and nothing happens, because no rung reads it. An HMI only asks; the program decides.

The Operator View

Window → Open Operator View, the Operator View under the simulator in the organizer, or HMI in the phone’s bottom bar. A row of buttons across the top switches screens in one tap; on the bottle line they are the line’s console, the mix tank, the case packer, the camera, the tanks, the totes and the feeders. Beside the screen is a control panel: a RUNNING lamp, an ALARM lamp, START and STOP (with the tag each writes under it, in red if there is no such tag) and a message line. Each screen keeps its own tags, and the first time you switch to one, the view takes them from the Process HMI on the floor that shows it. The buttons work in Run mode; in Program mode they say so and do nothing.

The packer’s screen has START, STOP, Running and its case counts; a camera has no START or STOP, because it runs when the PLC enables triggering, so its panel keeps only ON LINE and ALARM.

Recipes: what goes in, what stays out

A real batch tank is never trusted to the program alone to keep the wrong liquid out. The mix tank has the interlocks built in, the way a plant puts them in the pump starter circuit: a pump on a locked inlet does not run, even with its output on, and the MAIN page shows A LOCKED or B LOCKED in red. The RECIPE page is where the operator sets the batch up before START.

A supply tote holds an ingredient: water, cola syrup, lemon-lime syrup, flavour concentrate, orange or apple concentrate, milk or oil. A product is made from its ingredients in the tank, to a recipe. Picking a product on the PRODUCT card loads its line of this table into the tank and the setpoint tag, and sets the mode to AUTO:

The MODE decides which inlets a batch uses: AUTO (whatever the recipe calls for), MIX A+B, A ONLY, B ONLY, SAME LIQUID (inlet B draws through a crossover from A’s source, so the tank fills twice as fast) and WATER RINSE. On top of the mode come three locks no mode lifts: contamination (oil and the water-based liquids never meet, and the tank remembers what is in it until it is emptied or purged), lockout / tagout (LOCK on the page, or Locked out on a tote, until someone unlocks it), and purging. Once a batch is in the tank and the process is running, the recipe is locked (Recipe locked: a batch is in cycle) until it is stopped, purged or finished; START, STOP, PURGE and the inlet locks stay live, because lockout is a safety function and is never locked out itself. PURGE drains the tank to the floor drain on demand, after asking, and the batch is discarded.

Try it: water when water is called for

On Level 7 with its reference program, open the Operator View and the RECIPE page. With the batch stopped, pick WATER: inlet B goes LOCKED. Press START: water doses as before, but when the program turns on PumpB nothing comes in, the Simulator Log says why, and the sequence waits for a HI probe that never comes. The program asked; the interlock said no. Stop, pick SAME LIQUID and start again: inlet B runs water from Supply_A and the tank fills.
